btcStrategy.title: BTC Strategy
btcStrategy.applyHint: After changing parameters, apply them to recalculate the current zone and chart.
btcStrategy.noTemplateParameters: This template has no manual parameters.
btcStrategy.referenceReturnNote: Returns use Web daily data as a reference calculation for comparison with Buy & Hold. They are not the AutoQuant/FreqTrade experiment returns or a precise trading backtest.
btcStrategy.loadFailed: Failed to load BTC strategy data.

parameterHelp.momentumDays: How many daily periods to compare CBBI/AHR999 momentum against.
parameterHelp.exitMomentumDays: How many daily periods to use when judging fading CBBI momentum.
parameterHelp.cbbiEntryMax: CBBI must be below this value before the strategy can enter a DCA buy zone.
parameterHelp.entryAhrMax: AHR999 must be below this value before CbbiAhr999Daily can enter a DCA buy zone.
parameterHelp.exitMomentumThreshold: Momentum strategies enter a DCA sell zone when CBBI momentum falls below this value.
parameterHelp.exitCbbi: CBBI above this value is treated as cycle heat and enters a DCA sell zone.
parameterHelp.exitAhr: AHR999 above this value is treated as valuation heat and enters a DCA sell zone.
parameterHelp.hardStopEnabled: Off by default for spot zone reading. When enabled it affects only reference trade returns, not zone colors.
parameterHelp.stoplossPct: When hard stop is enabled, reference trades exit at this drawdown, such as -25 for a 25% drop.
parameterHelp.trendFastDays: Fast trend EMA period. Values with existing EMA series, like 50, 100, and 200, are most accurate.
parameterHelp.trendSlowDays: Slow trend period, usually used to judge whether the major trend is broken.

cbbi_momentum_opt.logic: Waits for CBBI to recover from low levels instead of waiting for fear alone, with EMA100 above EMA200.
cbbi_momentum_opt.entry: DCA buy zone when CBBI is below the cap, 3-day momentum turns positive, and fast trend is above slow trend.
cbbi_momentum_opt.exit: DCA sell zone when CBBI momentum fades, CBBI overheats, or the fast trend falls below the slow trend.
cbbi_momentum_opt.bestFor: Trend repair phases, especially after a larger BTC bottom starts to resolve.
cbbi_momentum_opt.note: The AutoQuant version used a 1h experiment setup and stoploss. This Web version is a daily spot zone model.

cbbi_momentum.logic: Uses low CBBI momentum recovery as the main signal, focusing more on direction than a static cheap threshold.
cbbi_momentum.entry: CBBI below the cap with positive momentum and a passing trend filter.
cbbi_momentum.exit: DCA sell zone when CBBI momentum fades, CBBI overheats, or trend breaks.
cbbi_momentum.bestFor: Users who want a simpler BTC cycle momentum view.
cbbi_momentum.note: It is more raw than the Opt version and may miss fast reversals more easily.

cbbi_ahr999_daily.logic: Combines CBBI cycle heat with AHR999 valuation to find daily low-valuation recovery zones.
cbbi_ahr999_daily.entry: DCA buy zone when both CBBI and AHR999 are low and both momentum values turn positive.
cbbi_ahr999_daily.exit: DCA sell zone when CBBI or AHR999 moves above its exit threshold.
cbbi_ahr999_daily.bestFor: Spot users who want both cycle temperature and valuation temperature.
cbbi_ahr999_daily.note: This is a daily indicator mix and should not be interpreted as hourly trading behavior.

smart_hold.logic: Bull-market hold template that reduces exposure only when the long trend breaks.
smart_hold.entry: Stays active when volume is valid and the trend is not broken.
smart_hold.exit: DCA sell zone when the fast EMA is below the slow EMA and price is below SMA200.
smart_hold.bestFor: Users who want fewer switches and care mainly about major trend holding.
smart_hold.note: This is more of a major-trend position template than a bottom-fishing strategy.

bear01.logic: Uses SMA200 as a simple bull/bear divider to protect exposure below the long average.
bear01.entry: Allows holding when price is above SMA200.
bear01.exit: DCA sell zone when price falls below SMA200.
bear01.bestFor: Users who want a simple long-term trend filter.
bear01.note: Funding and stablecoin filters from AutoQuant are not wired into the Web version yet.

buy_and_hold.logic: Buy once and hold, serving as the baseline for strategy return comparison.
buy_and_hold.bestFor: Checking whether a strategy actually improves on long-term holding.
buy_and_hold.note: If hard stop is enabled, it is no longer a pure Buy & Hold baseline.

tip.trailingPE: Price divided by earnings over the past 12 months. Lower PE may indicate undervaluation; higher PE may signal overvaluation or high growth expectations.
tip.forwardPE: Price divided by estimated future earnings. Lower than trailing PE suggests analysts expect earnings growth.
tip.pegRatio: PE divided by earnings growth rate. PEG < 1 may indicate the stock is undervalued relative to its growth.
tip.divYield: Annual dividend as a percentage of stock price. Higher yield means more income per dollar invested.
tip.marketCap: Total market value of a company's shares. Large-cap (>$10B) is typically more stable; small-cap (<$2B) is higher risk/reward.
tip.grossMargin: Revenue minus cost of goods, divided by revenue. Shows how much profit remains after production costs.
tip.profitMargin: Net income divided by revenue. Shows how much of each dollar in sales becomes profit after all expenses.
tip.revenueGrowth: Year-over-year change in total sales. Positive growth indicates expanding business.
tip.pbRatio: Price divided by book value per share. P/B < 1 may indicate undervaluation; common in banks and financials.
tip.beta: Measures stock volatility relative to the market. Beta > 1 means more volatile; < 1 means less volatile than S&P 500.
tip.roe: Return on Equity: net income / shareholder equity. Measures how efficiently a company generates profit from invested capital.
tip.deRatio: Total debt divided by shareholder equity. Higher ratio means more leverage and higher financial risk.
tip.cape: Cyclically-adjusted PE using 10-year average inflation-adjusted earnings. Smooths out business cycles for long-term valuation.
tip.earningsYield: Inverse of PE ratio (1/PE). Can be compared to bond yields to assess relative attractiveness of stocks vs bonds.
tip.atmIV: At-the-money Implied Volatility: the market's expected annualized price swing. Higher IV = more expensive options.
tip.rv20d: Realized Volatility over 20 trading days: how much the stock actually moved recently.
tip.rv60d: Realized Volatility over 60 trading days: a longer-term measure of actual price movement.
tip.ivRv: IV/RV ratio: compares expected vs actual volatility. >1.3 means options are expensive (IV rich); <0.8 means cheap (IV cheap).
tip.pcOI: Put/Call Open Interest ratio: total put OI / total call OI. >1.0 signals more bearish positioning; <0.5 signals bullish positioning.
tip.pcVol: Put/Call Volume ratio: today's put volume / call volume. Shows real-time directional sentiment.
tip.ivTerm: IV at different expirations. Normally longer-dated IV is higher (contango). If near-term IV is higher, it's backwardation — often signals an upcoming event.
tip.callWall: Strike with the highest call open interest. Acts as potential resistance — large OI can pin price near this level.
tip.putWall: Strike with the highest put open interest. Acts as potential support — large OI can pin price near this level.
tip.strike: The price at which the option can be exercised. In-the-money (ITM) options have intrinsic value; out-of-the-money (OTM) do not.
tip.iv: Implied Volatility: the market's forecast of future price movement, priced into the option. Higher IV = pricier option.
tip.oi: Open Interest: total number of outstanding contracts. High OI at a strike indicates significant positioning.
tip.vol: Trading volume: number of contracts traded today. High volume suggests active interest.
tip.bidAsk: Bid is the highest price a buyer will pay; Ask is the lowest a seller will accept. Narrower spread = more liquid.
tip.ivSkew: Shows how IV varies across strike prices. Put IV is usually higher (volatility smile) — reflects demand for downside protection.
tip.fearGreed: Gauges market sentiment from 0 (Extreme Fear) to 100 (Extreme Greed). Based on VIX level — low VIX = greed, high VIX = fear.
tip.yieldCurve: Plots Treasury yields by maturity. A normal curve slopes upward. An inverted curve (short > long) historically signals recession risk.
tip.hySpread: Yield difference between high-yield (junk) bonds and Treasuries. Widening spreads signal rising credit risk and risk aversion.
tip.igSpread: Yield difference between investment-grade corporate bonds and Treasuries. A safer credit barometer than HY.
tip.netLiquidity: Fed Balance Sheet minus TGA and Reverse Repo. Rising net liquidity tends to support asset prices.
tip.fedBalanceSheet: Total assets held by the Federal Reserve. Expansion (QE) injects liquidity; contraction (QT) removes it.
tip.fedFundsRate: The interest rate at which banks lend to each other overnight. The Fed's primary tool for monetary policy.
tip.tga: Treasury General Account: the government's checking account at the Fed. Drawdowns release liquidity into the market.
tip.reverseRepo: Overnight Reverse Repo: cash parked at the Fed by money market funds. High RRP means excess liquidity sitting on the sidelines.
tip.m2: Broad money supply including cash, deposits, and money market funds. M2 growth supports economic activity and asset prices.
tip.vix: CBOE Volatility Index: measures expected 30-day S&P 500 volatility. VIX < 15 = calm; 20-30 = elevated; > 30 = high fear.
tip.claims: Weekly count of new unemployment benefit filings. Rising claims signal labor market weakness.
tip.cpi: Consumer Price Index: measures average change in prices paid by consumers. The primary inflation gauge.
tip.corePCE: Core Personal Consumption Expenditures: excludes food and energy. The Fed's preferred inflation measure.
tip.spread10y2y: Difference between 10-year and 2-year Treasury yields. Negative = inverted curve, a classic recession signal.
tip.regime: Composite market health signal from 6 dimensions. Each metric's percentile rank over 1 year determines the signal level.

chartGuide.cape: Above the mean line → market is expensive by historical standards. Below → relatively cheap. Extreme peaks often precede major corrections.
chartGuide.trailingPE: Rising trend → market getting more expensive. Above mean → elevated valuation. Sharp drops often coincide with recessions.
chartGuide.forwardPE: Rising → market pricing in optimism. Divergence from trailing PE shows earnings growth expectations.
chartGuide.VIXCLS: Spikes = market panic (good contrarian buy signals). Sustained low VIX (<15) = complacency, may precede a volatility shock.
chartGuide.T10Y2Y: Below zero (yellow line) = yield curve inverted → recession warning. Steepening back above zero often signals recovery ahead.
chartGuide.BAMLH0A0HYM2: Rising = credit stress, investors demanding more compensation for risk. Spikes above 600 bps often signal severe risk-off.
chartGuide.M2SL: Rising = money supply expanding, generally supportive for stocks and the economy. Flat or declining = tightening liquidity.
chartGuide.ICSA: Rising trend = labor market weakening. Sustained above 300K is a warning sign. Spikes often lead recessions.
chartGuide.CPIAUCSL: Steepening slope = inflation accelerating. Flattening = inflation cooling. The Fed tightens when this rises too fast.
chartGuide.netLiquidity: Rising = more money flowing into markets, supportive for asset prices. Falling = liquidity drain, headwind for stocks.
chartGuide.yieldCurve: Normal: upward slope (long rates > short). Flat or inverted: the bond market is pricing in an economic slowdown or recession.
